title: Lusin's theorem for Borel maps ℝⁿ → L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) on Borel sets of finite measure
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ (volume). Let F : ℝⁿ → L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) be Borel measurable, where L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) is the space of continuous linear maps ℝⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm and its Borel σ-algebra. Let S ⊆ ℝⁿ be a Borel set with Lⁿ(S) < ∞ and let δ ∈ (0, ∞]. Then there is a closed set C ⊆ S with Lⁿ(S \ C) < δ such that F is continuous on C.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] ℝ)), Measurable F → ∀ S : Set (Rn n), MeasurableSet S → volume S ≠ ∞ → ∀ δ : ℝ≥0∞, δ ≠ 0 → ∃ C : Set (Rn n), C ⊆ S ∧ IsClosed C ∧ volume (S \ C) < δ ∧ ContinuousOn F C
